methods.description: Find shared-factor LCD, rewrite equivalent fractions and compare, including improper/equal contrasts.
For denominators with only common factor1, use their product, rewrite both fractions and compare.
Convert mixed numbers to improper when present, use one denominator and order; return original form.
Compare candidate fractions with both interval endpoints; strict between excludes equal endpoints.
Identify simple fractional distance below/above a whole number and compare those distances using equivalence; indirect source application.

7.  Arrange these fractions in ascending order by:

    a.  Expressing as improper fractions:
        .......................................

    b.  Determining the LCD: .......................................

    c.  Rewriting fractions with the LCD:
        .......................................

    d.  Ordering the fractions by comparing numerators:
        .......................................

    e.  Rewriting fractions back in their original form.
        .......................................

sourceReview.observation: Complete five-fraction mixed/improper ordering scaffold read. It explicitly converts mixed to improper, findsLCD, rewrites and orders, then returns original form. Nearest-to-integer is an indirect application: identify the remaining fraction of one whole or the fractional part above the integer, then compare those fractions with this same route; no decimal approximation or general fraction-operation method needed. Not claimed a filled source closest example.
sourceReview.adjustments: E2 adapts full mixed ordering scaffold with manageable new fractions. E4 is explicitly indirect complementary-parts application, using simple one-whole reasoning and comparison of distances; original closest question preserved with exact fraction working and wrong-option reasons.

substantiveCorrections: Qualify blanket fact: same denominator permits direct numerator comparison, without falsely claiming all other comparisons impossible.
